record.what_it_does: Messaging platform with an HTTP Bot API and MTProto user-client API.
record.auth_notes: Bot API: each bot gets a token from @BotFather, which is passed in the URL path (api.telegram.org/bot<token>/METHOD). MTProto user API: api_id/api_hash from my.telegram.org, then login by phone code (auth.sendCode), 2FA via SRP, or a QR-code login token. Bots can also log in over MTProto with auth.importBotAuthorization. Telegram now offers 'Log In with Telegram', a standard OIDC authorization-code flow with PKCE (oauth.telegram.org; scopes openid, profile, phone, telegram:bot_access). It gives identity only. Its one extra power is letting your bot DM the user. It does not grant API access to the user's chats, so it is not listed as an API auth method. A multi-user toolkit would use bot tokens. Acting as a user needs an MTProto session, with ban risk. Business Mode is a middle path: a user connects a bot to their account and chooses which chats it can access, but this needs Telegram Business (Premium).
record.access_notes: Bot tokens are free and instant via @BotFather, with no review. api_id/api_hash is free at my.telegram.org. Each phone number can have only one api_id. Third-party clients must follow the API Terms of Service. All accounts that log in through unofficial API clients are automatically put under observation, and flooding or spam leads to a permanent ban. Business Mode bot connections require the end user to have Telegram Business/Premium.
record.api_breadth_notes: The Bot API is an HTTP API (GET/POST against api.telegram.org, currently version 10.5, dated 2026-11-22). It has 100+ methods covering messages, media, chats and members, inline mode, payments and Stars, stickers, business connections, Mini Apps and games. It can also run as a self-hosted Local Bot API Server. MTProto is a separate binary RPC protocol (not REST) with a full user-client method set, wrapped by the TDLib library. I did not count the methods exactly.
record.mcp_notes: No official Telegram MCP server was found. Community MTProto/user-account servers: chigwell/telegram-mcp (Telethon), sparfenyuk/mcp-telegram, overpod/mcp-telegram (GramJS), lexfrei/mcp-tg (Go), l1v0n1/telegram-mcp-server. There are also community Bot API-token servers.
record.blocker_notes: There is no delegated OAuth for API access. OIDC login gives identity and bot-DM permission only. Bots see only chats where they were started or added, or the chats a Business user explicitly connects (Premium only). Acting as a user requires an MTProto phone or QR login with ban monitoring and ToS risk. In a multi-user toolkit, each user would supply their own bot token.
